title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-02-28
source: flac16/48kHz; Ampex MM-1000 16 Track Master Reels Two Inch Wide Tape @ 15 ips; Multi Track Mix-down To a Sony PCM 1630 By Dan Healy @ 44.1KHz); Set #1 DAT x ONE by Dick Latvala-DAT x TWO; Set #2 DAT x ? by Rob Bertrando-DAT x; Editing(Adobe Audition CC)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name)-Sample Rate Conversion(r8brain); This is a 100% Flat transfer from the DAT no signal processing what-so-ever. Some pitch correction implemented Jim Wise

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1969‑02‑28 performance with a monster Alligator suite, School Girl and The Other One, captured in a crisp multi‑track soundboard mix (with minor pitch quirks).
ai_review.review: The show is widely hailed as a "monster" night – the 30‑minute Alligator jam, a scorching Good Morning School Girl, and powerhouse renditions of The Other One and Death Don't Have No Mercy dominate the setlist. The multi‑track soundboard source delivers clear imaging and strong instrument separation, though a few reviewers note occasional speed/pitch wobble in the recording. Overall the musical performance is stellar and the recording more than listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both performance (many 5‑star remarks, standout jams) and recording quality; only minor technical complaints keep the rating just below top tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp multi‑track mix with excellent instrument separation; a few reviewers mention patchy sections and slight speed/pitch wobble in the drums/Alligator segment, but overall clear and listenable.

standout_songs: Alligator > Drums > Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) > Feedback > And We Bid You Good Night
show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑set marathon that builds from a blues‑heavy first set into an improvisational second set and culminates in the epic Alligator suite; transitions are praised as seamless and the pacing stays intense throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for flowing ideas, prominent mix and strong guitar work throughout the night.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass highlighted especially on The Eleven and The Other One, often described as 'owning' the jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard contributions noted as tight and inspired, particularly on Love Light and during the Alligator improvisations.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums segment praised for power; a few recordings show minor speed/pitch wobble but performance remains solid.
